message: `dispatch` claims `restrict(no-escape)` and the claim cannot be checked: the body calls a value the compiler could not resolve - a parameter, a closure or a field - so where its allocations flow is not something the walk can settle
help: a limit of the ANALYSIS rather than a defect in the program - AX3037's argument at one remove. There are three readings: an effect present only as POSSIBLE, a row the walk marked incomplete, and a body that CALLS one of its own parameters (`#effect-params=`), whose answer is chosen by each caller and cannot be settled here at all. Name the function at the call, stop calling the parameter, or drop the claim; `no-cast` and `no-wrap` are checked regardless, because both are lexical and need no call resolved

message: `stores` claims `restrict(no-escape)` and the body stores a value it allocates into its parameter `v` through `vecPush`
help: a restriction is a CLAIM the author wrote, and this is the compiler answering it. `no-io`, `no-alloc`, `no-foreign`, `no-cast:deep` and `no-recursion` are transitive - the effect row and the call graph are fixpoints over every callee - and the path in the message is the chain of resolved calls (`symbols --calls` spells each hop the same way) from this declaration to where the effect enters, or around the cycle, so the fix is at a named place rather than somewhere below. Make the body keep the claim, or delete the tag, which WITHDRAWS the claim rather than answering it; an unrestricted function is never asked

message: `dispatchStrict` claims `restrict(no-escape, strict)` and the claim cannot be PROVEN: the body calls a value the compiler could not resolve - a parameter, a closure or a field - so where its allocations flow is not something the walk can settle
help: `strict` asks for a guarantee and not a best effort: where the walk cannot settle the claim, it is refused rather than warned. The three readings are AX3051's - an effect present only as POSSIBLE, a row the walk marked incomplete, and a body that CALLS one of its own parameters (`#effect-params=`), whose answer is chosen by each caller. Name the function at the call site, stop calling the parameter, or drop `strict` to keep the claim as a checked best effort (AX3051)
